topics.label: Lecture introduction and complement framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic opens the lecture by establishing the context, complexity, and importance of studying the complement system.

topics.label: Foundations and core principles of the complement cascade
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental organization, naming conventions, and central biochemical role of C3 in the complement system.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three upstream recognition pathways that drive C3 convertase activity and reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Downstream effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three primary effector outcomes triggered by complement activation to eliminate pathogens and promote inflammation.

topics.label: Host cell regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory mechanisms and proteins that protect host tissues from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the distinct disease presentations and immunopathologies resulting from deficiencies in individual complement factors.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion strategies and practical applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how pathogens circumvent complement defenses and how these bacterial evasion proteins are utilized in medicine and research.

topics.label: Lecture closing and upcoming topics
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the next session on the adaptive immune system.
